thread:
Columbia is in New York City, and it's still not #1.

We counted every place to eat within a 10-minute walk (half a mile) of each Ivy League campus. Here's the ranking:

1. Yale: 223
2. Columbia: 214
3. Harvard: 156
4. Brown: 133
5. Penn: 125
6. Princeton: 97
7. Cornell: 69
8. Dartmouth: 39

Measured from each campus's center, using Overture Maps listings.

Look up any campus, with the closest places first: https://www.savorscout.net/campus/

At UNC Chapel Hill, 70% of the places to eat within a mile of campus are on one street: Franklin Street.

We checked which big universities have the biggest share of their restaurants on a single street.

Universities with 20,000+ students and at least 100 places to eat within a mile:

U. of Delaware, Main St: 73%
UNC, Franklin St: 70%
UC Riverside, University Ave: 66%
Cal State Northridge, Reseda Blvd: 66%
U. of New Mexico, Central Ave: 66%

Next: University of Maryland, Baltimore Ave (63%), Michigan State, Grand River Ave (60%), and NC State, Hillsborough St (53%).

Big cities are the opposite. Near NYU, the street with the most places to eat has just 4% of them.

We counted the places to eat in Overture Maps' listings within a mile of each campus's center, by street address.

How to tell whether a dumpling place makes its own dumplings, before you order:

Look at the wrappers. Handmade ones are a little uneven: thicker at the pleats, thin in the middle. Machine-made wrappers are perfectly even and usually thicker.

You can see the difference before you taste it.
Potstickers and gyoza should be crisp on the bottom and soft on top. All soft means they were only steamed. All hard means they were fried from frozen.

Soup dumplings should hold their soup. One or two leaking in the basket is normal. All of them is not.

And the best sign of all: people folding dumplings in the window.

The menu tells you too. Look for a short list done well, or a full dim sum menu. A general restaurant with a dumpling section is the one to skip.

What to order, from soup dumplings to momo: https://www.savorscout.net/food/dumplings

A lot of boba is just sugar with pearls in it. Here's how to find a shop that actually makes tea.

The pearls should be chewy with a soft center, since cooked tapioca is only good for about four hours. The tea should be brewed, not powdered. And the shop should ask how sweet you want it.

Trying a new shop? Order a classic milk tea at 50% sugar. If that's good, everything else will be.
